2608.25693.title: Unsupervised Anatomical Feature Learning via Diffusion Models: Enhanced Medical Image Segmentation with Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
2608.25693.paper_summary: Acquiring pixel-level annotations for medical image segmentation is a severe bottleneck. Traditional U-Net architectures, while effective, learn local texture patterns and lack awareness of global anatomical structures, leading to boundary delineation failures in low-data regimes. This research paper proposes utilizing unsupervised Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPMs) to extract anatomical features. We train a DDPM on 21 unlabeled abdominal CT scans to learn structural representations, transferring the encoder weights to a downstream segmentation task evaluated on the BTCV multi-organ dataset. Diffusion pretraining significantly improved liver segmentation: Dice increased from $0.75\pm0.36$ to $0.93\pm0.16$ ($p < 5.33\times10^{-26}$, 0.529 Cohen's d), Average Surface Distance (ASD) decreased by 66%, and 95th-percentile Hausdorff Distance (HD95) reduced by 45%. For kidney segmentation, Dice improved from $0.90\pm0.19$ to $0.95\pm0.10$ ($p < 4.01\times10^{-11}$). Multi-organ pooled performance showed a 68% variance reduction and a 74% improvement in boundary precision (Dice $0.95\pm0.07$). Crucially, frozen encoder models retained > 80% of fine-tuned performance without exposure to segmentation labels, proving the existence of learned anatomical priors. In low-data scenarios, diffusion-pretrained models maintained robust performance with only 50% (Dice: 0.92 liver, 0.94 kidney), 25%, and even 10% (Dice: 0.89 liver, 0.71 kidney) of labeled data. Using unlabeled images for diffusion-based pretraining successfully embeds robust anatomical features prior to human supervision, transforming U-Nets into anatomy-aware systems.
2608.25693.paper_summary_zh: 獲取醫學影像分割的像素級註釋是一個嚴重的瓶頸。傳統的 U-Net 架構雖然有效，但學習的是局部紋理模式，缺乏對全局解剖結構的認識，導致在低數據環境下邊界劃分失敗。本研究論文提出利用無監督去噪擴散概率模型 (DDPMs) 來提取解剖特徵。我們在 21 個未標記的腹部 CT 掃描上訓練 DDPM，以學習結構表示，並將編碼器權重轉移到下游的分割任務中，該任務在 BTCV 多器官數據集上進行評估。擴散預訓練顯著改善了肝臟分割：Dice 從 $0.75\pm0.36$ 增加到 $0.93\pm0.16$ ($p < 5.33\times10^{-26}$, 0.529 Cohen's d)，平均表面距離 (ASD) 減少了 66%，而第 95 百分位的豪斯多夫距離 (HD95) 減少了 45%。對於腎臟分割，Dice 從 $0.90\pm0.19$ 提高到 $0.95\pm0.10$ ($p < 4.01\times10^{-11}$)。多器官的綜合性能顯示出 68% 的方差減少和 74% 的邊界精度改善 (Dice $0.95\pm0.07$)。關鍵是，凍結的編碼器模型在未接觸分割標籤的情況下保留了 > 80% 的微調性能，證明了學習到的解剖先驗的存在。在低數據場景中，擴散預訓練模型在僅使用 50% (Dice: 0.92 肝臟, 0.94 腎臟)、25% 甚至 10% (Dice: 0.89 肝臟, 0.71 腎臟) 的標記數據下保持了穩健的性能。使用未標記的影像進行基於擴散的預訓練成功地嵌入了穩健的解剖特徵，並在人工監督之前轉變了 U-Net 成為具備解剖認知的系統。
